# Temple Scroll Column 43 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 43 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**43:1** Every animal that walks on its paws — any four-footed creature with paws — is unclean to you.

**43:2** Anyone who touches their dead body becomes unclean until evening.

**43:3** Anyone who picks up their dead body must wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. These animals are unclean to you.

**43:4** Among the small creatures that crawl on the ground, these are unclean to you: the weasel, the rat, every kind of large lizard,

**43:5** the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.

**43:6** Anyone who touches their dead body becomes unclean until evening; anyone who picks up their dead body must wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening.

**43:7** If any of these creatures falls on something after it dies, that object becomes unclean — whether it is a wooden tool, a piece of clothing, a leather item, or a sack.

**43:8** Any tool used for work must be soaked in water and will remain unclean until evening; after that it is clean.

**43:9** If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it becomes unclean — break the pot.

**43:10** Any food that gets wet from such water becomes unclean, and any drink in such a container becomes unclean.

**43:11** Every creature that crawls along the ground is disgusting — do not eat it.

**43:12** Whether it slithers on its belly, walks on all fours, or has many legs — do not eat any creature that swarms on the ground. They are all disgusting.

**43:13** Do not make yourselves disgusting by eating any swarming creature, and do not make yourselves unclean through them.

**43:14** For I am the LORD your God. Set yourselves apart and be holy, because I am holy.

**43:15** Do not defile yourselves with any creature that crawls on the ground.

**43:16** For I am the LORD who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, because I am holy.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column forbids eating or touching the carcasses of various crawling and swarming creatures, paralleling Leviticus 11. The specific animal identifications are debated among scholars — ancient Hebrew names do not always map neatly to modern taxonomy. The theological climax is striking: the reason for these dietary rules is God's own holiness and his desire for his people to reflect it.*
